blocks.content: India is an indestructible Union of destructible states.

items: A bill altering state boundaries under Article 3 requires the prior recommendation of the President before introduction in Parliament.
The views expressed by a State Legislature regarding its boundary alteration are purely advisory and not binding on Parliament.
Cession of Indian territory to a foreign country cannot be done under Article 3; it requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368 (Berubari Union Case, 1960).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 1 describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States'.
Article 2 grants Parliament the power to admit into the Union or establish new states that were not previously part of India.
Article 3 authorizes Parliament to reorganize existing internal state boundaries, areas, or names through a simple majority.
Article 4 specifies that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not considered constitutional amendments under Article 368.
The Fazl Ali Commission (1953) broadly accepted language as the basis for reorganization of states, giving rise to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
